Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The Australian players are seen raring to go on the sidelines as the umpires make their way out to the middle. Tammy Beaumont and Amy Jones are the openers for England. Megan Schutt has the new ball in hand and is ready to steam in. Let's go...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then! England Women need 311 runs to win and break the record for the most successful run-chase in Women's World Cup history. New Zealand did come close to breaking it last night but it seems to be a much tougher job tonight against a feisty Australian bowling attack. Can England pull off a miracle? The run-chase coming up next.

Meg Lanning is up for a quick chat. Lanning says it was hard at the front as England bowled really well. Adds that Haynes took the pressure away from her and they built the innings really well at the back end. Mentions the pitch was hard but it was flat as the game progressed, there was some dampness, and hopes her bowlers can bowl well on it.

Heather Knight won the toss and elected to bowl first which was the correct decision given the conditions and also the slowness of the outfield. The Aussie openers, especially Healy attacked the English pacers right from the off. They did manage to get Healy out but failed to capitalize on it. Knight will be lamenting the fact that her side wasn't daring enough to take a few more risks and allowed the pair of Lanning and Haynes to get settled in nicely. This proved to be fatal as even the experienced trio of Sciver, Shrubsole and Brunt couldn't get control in the middle overs. The final few overs produced a lot of runs and having just 5 regulations bowlers didn't help England either. Sophie Ecclestone had to bowl at the death and the spinner was taken to the cleaners in the end. All in all a disappointing bowling effort and now the batters have a tough job on their hands.

There was rain early in the day and the wicket wasn't the easiest to bat on. Alyssa Healy and Rachael Haynes tried to get Australia off to a flier but the feisty Healy fell early after scoring a few boundaries. After Healy departed, it was up to the captain and the vice-captain to do the repair work and boy didn't they do it to the tee. It was slow going for a long period of time as both Haynes and Lanning just tried to find their feet. Once they got set, they took on the English bowlers and made sure that the bad deliveries were put away. The pair put on a partnership of 196-runs and Rachael Haynes even went on to get a big century. After Meg Lanning was sent back, Beth Mooney came out with aggressive intent and Ellyse Perry too joined the party in the final over to guide their side to a daunting total.

What a blistering start to the Women's World Cup we have had! It was Hayley Matthews last night and today it is Rachael Haynes with the big-match innings. Australia Women have ended up with 310 runs on a pitch that isn't the easiest to bat on and an outfield which isn't the quickest either. What an effort! England Women have their work cut out in front of them and it will require something special from their batters to chase this mammoth total down.
A single! Flatter and on middle, tucked to square leg for a single. Australia Women end their innings at 310/3.
FOUR! What a cameo this is turning out to be! Tossed up, on middle. Ellyse Perry sweeps it to deep square leg for yet another boudary. Ellyse Perry giving the finishing touches.
FOUR! Flatter and outside off. Ellyse Perry dabs it hard and to third man for a boundary. The fielder gives a chase but in vain.
Tossed up, on middle. Mooney works it to mid-wicket for a single.
300 up for Australia Women! A single as this is hit to point.
FOUR!  Perry was waiting for some time to get out. This is what she wanted to show! On a length, on the pads. Perry tickles it past the diving fine leg fielder for a boundary.
FOUR! Short and outside off. Mooney slaps it over point for a boundary.
Ellyse Perry is in at number 5.

OUT! TAKEN! Haynes goes! From the start and almost finished the innings! What a special innings from her. Nothing wrong by her, she tried to finish on high as Haynes tries to heave this full delivery over mid-wicket but fails to power. Danni Wyatt there takes it. Haynes goes with appreciation from everyone on the ground and gets some from England players as well. Fantastic innings from her.
Commentary.Howout: c Danni Wyatt b Natalie Sciver

Commentary.Commentary: Another superb yorker but Mooney is equal to the task as she gets her bat in middle and hits it to point for one.
Short of a length, on middle, pulled to deep square leg for a single.
A yorker, on middle. Haynes guides it nicely but finds point.
SIX! Freebie to start! A full toss, on middle. Haynes had all the time as she pulls it well over square leg for a biggie. Nearing to 150...
On middle, this is hit to square leg for a single.

In the air and drops safely! Tossed up, on middle. Haynes steps down and looks to go big but mistimes it straight down the ground. The ball drops before the fielder from long on can comes across. Two taken.
Around off, Mooney smashes it to extra cover for a single.
A single as this is hit t o long on.

Dropped! Hard chance though! Tossed up, on middle. Haynes does not reach to the pitch of the ball. Still hits it towards long on. Natalie Sciver runs across from mid-wicket and dives but fails to catch it. Two taken.
On the pads, nudged on the leg side for a leg bye as it came off the pads.
FOUR! What a shot! Fuller ball, on middle. Haynes heaves it in the gap, to mid-wicket for a boundary. Started the over with a boundary and ended with the same.
Short again, on middle. Haynes shuffles away on the leg side and works it over the keeper. Two runs taken this time. Body language suggests England are exhausted now.
A low dipping full toss, down the leg side. Haynes misses her sweep. Not given as a wide.
Length ball, angling on the pads, tucked on the leg side for a single.
Full and on middle, flicked to deep square leg for a couple of r uns.
FOUR! A slower short ball, on middle. Mooney backs away and ramps it over backward point for a boundary. Played with the field there.
Fuller and on leg, drilled to long on for one.
Flatter and on off, it is hit to point for a single.
FOUR! Glorious shot! Tossed up, on off. Haynes makes room and goes up and over covers for a boundary. Can Rachael Haynes get to 150?
FOUR! Floated ball, on middle. Haynes waits, and tries to paddle it but gets a top edge over the keeper and it races away to the fence. Rachael Haynes will take it anyday.
Tossed up, on middle and leg. Mooney skips down and drills it to long on for a single.
Fuller ball, on off, pushed to covers.
Sophie Ecclestone is brought back into the attack.
Slower delivery, around middle. Mooney uses her feet to ease it down to long on for a single. Australia have surpassed the 250-run mark. Can they get to 300 with 5 overs remaining?
A concussion protocol going on as Beth Mooney gets hit on the helmet. She looks absolutely fine and the play resumes.

Sciver with another short ball, around the helmet. Beth Mooney looks to pull but the ball hurries onto her. The ball hits the arm and then goes on to hit the helmet as well. Mandatory concussion check will now follow.
Too easy at the moment for the Aussie batters to pick up those singles. On a good length, around off and cutaway to point for a run.
Sliding down the leg side, flicked away towards fine leg for a single.
Shorter in length, on the body. Haynes pulls it down to deep square leg for one more.
Back of a length, outside off. This is steered through backward point for one.
Natalie Sciver is back on.
Full, on off. This is driven through cover for a single.

FIVE WIDES! Too many bonus runs from England and Heather Knight will not be pleased about that. Cross tries to cramp Mooney for room but spills it down the leg side. The ball evades everyone and runs away to the fine leg fence.
Around middle and leg, Mooney works it past square leg and races back for the second.
FOUR! Beth Mooney has come out with intent! Overpitched, on off and this is thumped right back over the bowler's head for a boundary.

There it is! A magnificent century for Rachael Haynes and what an innings this has been! Sliding down leg, just helped 'round the corner for a single. Haynes raises her bat and gets a standing ovation, deservingly so. A match-winning type performance from Haynes.
Drifted onto the pads, this is clipped through mid-wicket for a single.
On a good length, outside off. Haynes taps it towards point for a single and moves to 99.
Finally a breakthrough for England. The skipper goes after doing her job and now Beth Mooney will replace her.

OUT! TAKEN! Meg Lanning finds Tammy Beaumont and she cannot believe it! This is short and wide, there to be hit. Lanning rocks back and slaps it hard. The ball goes flat but straight to Tammy Beaumont at point. Beaumont didn't have to move an inch and takes a sharp catch. The skipper departs after another noteworthy innings and the 196-run stand is finally broken. Katherine Brunt gets a wicket off her final delivery and she is ecstatic.
Commentary.Howout: c Tammy Beaumont b Katherine Brunt

Commentary.Commentary: On a good length, angled into middle and leg. Haynes dabs it down to backward point for a run.
WIDE! Attempted short ball, angled at the body but slides down the leg side. Haynes looks to pull but misses. Wided.
Beaten! A touch fuller, around off. Haynes hangs back and tries to run it fine but misses.

This is banged in short around off. Meg Lanning takes on the pull shot but gets a top edge towards the square leg fence. Anya Shrubsole is quick to run around from deep backward square leg and keeps it down to a single.
This is wide of off stump, Haynes steers it down to third man for a run.
On a nagging length and targeting the pads. Lanning gets pushed back as she works it on the leg side for a single.
Cross comes from 'round the stumps and delivers a yorker on middle stump. Rachael Haynes makes room to cover drive but gets an inside edge past the leg stump towards short fine leg.
Full and wide, Lanning gets down on one knee and squeezes it out to deep point for a single.
Full, around off. This is driven to deep point for one more.
Tammy Beaumont is down holding her right shoulder. The physio quickly reaches and assists her. Looks fine and we are ready to resume.

Full and wide, this is slapped towards cover-point. Tammy Beaumont from point dives down to her right to get a hand on it and keeps it down to a single. She might have hurt her right shoulder though as she seems to be in pain.
Full and straight, drilled back past the bowler but without much timing. The fielder from mid off runs to her left and cuts it off. Just the single then.
A bit of width on offer but Haynes can't get it through cover-point.

SIX! High and handsome! A length ball, angling onto the hips. Meg Lanning just picks it up and launches it all the way over the square leg fence. The record partnership also comes on between these two. It's worth 187 at the moment.
Leg bye! This is fuller and angled into the pads. Rachael Haynes gets cramped for room as she looks to flick. The ball goes off the pads and rolls onto the leg side. They get a leg bye.
WIDE! Banged in and angled into the body. Haynes looks to pull but misses. The umpire signals a wide as the ball was just a bit down the leg side.
WIDE! Oh, dear! An attempted slower ball, spilled well down the leg side. Wide called.
Full and outside off, driven straight towards extra cover.
Length this time, around off and played past point for a run.
A bit shorter and wider, Lanning thumps it past the diving point fielder, who gets a hand on it for a couple of runs.
A well-directed short ball over middle. Lanning sways away from the line of the ball and Amy Jones makes a good grab behind the stumps.
A full toss, slightly high and on middle. Lanning miscues her pull to mid off for a single. Was very high but Natalie Sciver got away with it.
Short ball, outside off, dragged to deep mid-wicket for a single.
A slower ball, full and outside off, driven to sweeper cover for a single.
Sciver follows Haynes on the leg side and this is worked to square leg for a single.
Fuller ball, on middle, Lanning finds the gap at mid-wicket and takes a quick single. A shy at the bowler's end but the player misses.
Full toss, on middle. Haynes hits it to deep square leg for a single.
Short and on middle, pulled away to fine leg for one.

Leg bye! NOT OUT! Heather Knight was not that sure while taking it upstairs as they knew the result back of their mind. A full ball, angling middle and leg. Lanning misses her heave and gets hit on the pads. An appeal for LBW but the umpire is unmoved. The bowler convinces the skipper to take it upstairs. No bat there. Ball Tracking shows impact was umpire's call and the ball was angling down the leg side.

At this point, Heather Knight just had to go for DRS for an LBW decision. The third umpire checks UltraEdge and confirms that there's no bat involved. Ball Tracker shows the impact is umpire's call which doesn't even matter because the ball was sliding well down the leg side. A hopeful review but England Women lose a review in the end.
Steep bounce there, a bouncer, outside off. Lanning leaves it alone.
A full ball, angling around middle and leg. Lanning misses her flick and gets hit on the pads. An appeal for LBW but that was always going down.
Slower one, outside off. Rachael guides it to deep point for a single.
FOUR! Pressure on Brunt straightaway! Short in length, on middle. Haynes pulls it to square leg for a boundary. 200 up for Australia Women.
FOUR! Bang! Full ball, outside off. Lanning smashes it over mid off for a boundary. Both are eyeing the triple-digit score.
Short ball, outside off. Haynes hits it aerially over point for a single.
Full ball, on middle. Haynes wrists it over mid-wicket and the fielder from mid on charges to cut it off. Two taken.
A length ball, swinging in, outside off. Lanning chops it on the off side for a single.
Sciver follows Haynes on the leg side. She knocks it to point for a single.
FOUR!Good start to the over!Fuller ball, around off. Haynes makes room and drives it through covers for a boundary. 150-up between these two.
Natalie Sciver (5-0-19-1) is back on.
Fuller and on middle, pushed to mid on.
A length ball, outside off. Haynes dabs it fine to third man just for a single as the fielder does well to rush across.
Fuller and on middle. Lanning heaves it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Slightly short and this is pulled to deep mid-wicket  for one more.
On a length, on off, Lanning punches it through point for a run.
A single as Haynes dabs it to third man.
Flatter and outside off, guided to point.
Chance! Tossed up, on off. Haynes skips down and hammers it to the right of Ecclestone but this time she fails to get her right hand around. A single taken as it rolls to long off.
Full ball, outside off. Haynes smashes it straight back to Ecclestone and she gets her left hand stuck to it.
On the pads, flicked to mid-wicket for one.
FOUR! Sees a short ball and Lanning goes on the back foot, cuts it hard and beats the diving backward point fielder for a boundary.
Length ball, on off, this is hit to long on for a single.
Shorter in length and outside off. Haynes opens the face of the bat and guides it to deep backward point for another single.
Full, around off. This is driven on the up, through covers for a run.
WIDE! Anya Shrubsole goes for the yorker but spills it down the leg side. Amy Jones does really well to get her mitts behind that one.
A length ball, on off and jagging back in. Meg Lanning stays solid in defense.
Fullish delivery, around off. Rachael Haynes shuffles way across the stumps to get inside the line of the ball and paddle it down to fine leg for a single.
Slower, back of a length and outside off. Meg Lanning punches it off the back foot to deep cover for one.
On off, Lanning defends it out.
FOUR! Rachael Haynes is just finding the gaps at will right now. Short and wide, this is uppishly cutaway through the gap between point and backward point for another boundary.
Very full, down the leg side. Haynes looks to sweep it fine but misses and gets hit on the boot. A stifled appeal from the bowler and nothing more.
Slower through the air, outside off. Haynes gets behind the line of the ball to block.
This is pushed through a bit quicker, around off. Haynes pushes it towards covers.
FOUR! Flighted delivery, outside off and turning in. Rachael Haynes dances down the track and whacks it over extra cover for a boundary.
Quicker and flatter, on off. Lanning punches it towards covers off the back foot and picks up a run.
Sophie Ecclestone comes in for her second spell.

On middle and leg, tucked away to deep mid-wicket for another single. It's too easy at the moment for these two. England need to find some inspiration or else they could be staring down a mammoth total.
Fullish delivery, on the pads. Lanning gets pushed on the back foot as she keeps it out on the leg side.
Slower again, on a length and angled into the body. Haynes works it towards mid-wicket for a run.
Around off, Lanning bunts it out on the off side with soft hands and sets off for a quick single.
Haynes makes a bit of room leg side and Shrubsole follows her with a slower delivery. Haynes eases it behind point for a single.
Sliding onto the pads, flicked away towards square leg.
Full and wide, pushed out on the off side for a single.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries now for Rachael Haynes! Pitched up, around off. Haynes gives the charge and manages to get it through the cover-region for a boundary. 150 up now for Australia.

FOUR! The boundaries keep on coming and that is a cheeky shot from Rachael Haynes. Cross gets the yorker in on off stum from 'round the stump but Haynes exposes all three stumps and just jams it out fine. The ball runs away into the third man fence.
Very full, at the base of the off stump. Haynes backs away and squeezes it towards point.
Length this time, outside off. Lanning hangs back and steers it down to third man for one more.
Pitched up, on middle and skidding through. Haynes drives it through mid on for a single.

DRINKS! Fifty for both the batters out there at a very crucial time. That is the experience of Australia, they know how to progress on a difficult pitch. Slow start but starting to change the gears now. With wickets in hand, they will try and go big. Disappointment for England as they are finding it hard to get breakthroughs.

Rachael Haynes too gets to her fifty and the Aussies looking in command at the moment. Fullish ball, on middle. Haynes shuffles and works it towards fine leg for a single. She looked a bit edgy at the start but it's been free flowing for the past few overs.
Angled in from 'around the wicket. Haynes blocks it out on the off side.
This is slower from Anya Shrubsole and pushed wider. Lanning waits for it and slaps it to deep point for just a single.
On a good length, on off. Lanning looks to pull but gets a bottom edge and the ball goes nowhere.
Beaten! On a nagging length, outside off. Lanning just looks to run it down to third man but the ball skids on and she gets beaten past the outside edge.

Fifty for the classy Meg Lanning! A bit of width on offer and Lanning slashes it behind point for a brace. Came to bat on when the pith was difficult to play but she has shown her experience here. The skipper leads from the front in the World Cup.
On a length, nipping back in, and Lanning drops it to cover for yet another quick single.
Fuller ball, on off. Haynes drops it in front of covers and takes a quick single. Good running again.
A single as this is hit to point.
FOUR! Over mid on! Full ball, on middle. Meg Lanning looks to heave but mistimes her shot. Luckily for her, it goes well over mid on for a boundary. 100-run stand up as well.
Fuller ball, outside off. Lanning pushes it hard but straight to point.
Length ball, angling on the pads. Lanning looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads.
Kate Cross (6-0-25-0) is back on.
Length ball, around off. Meg works it to deep backward point and keeps the strike.
Fuller ball, at 101 kph, on middle. Defended on the front foot.
On a length, on off, tucked to mid-wicket for a quick single.
Around off, pulled away to square leg for a single.
FOUR! Into the 40s now! A length ball, outside off. Lanning opens the face of the bat and plays it late to third man. The fielder there puts a dive but the ball goes through her hands for a boundary.
Fuller ball, on off, pushed to mid off.
Anya Shrubsole (5-0-20-0) is brought back into the attack.
Length ball, drifting on middle. Haynes waits and dead-bats it.
Short ball, on middle. Lanning pulls it off the splice of the bat, to square leg for a single.
Length ball, around off. Lanning hops and blocks it out.
Length ball, outside off. Haynes dabs it to third man for one.
FOUR! Boundaries flowing easily now! Fuller ball, on off. Haynes steps across, gets low and scoops it through fine leg for a boundary.
Full ball, on off, this is hit to point.
FOUR! Freebie!  A full toss, down the leg side. Lanning gets low and helps it away to the fine leg fence for a boundary. Good end to the over for Australia.
On middle, swept behind square for a single.
Haynes presses to come down but changes her mind and stays back to defend it out.
Very full, on middle, pushed to covers for a single.
This one spins back in sharply, on middle. Haynes turns it to square leg for a single.
Fuller ball, outside off, pushed to sweeper cover for a single.
Length ball, angling outside off. Haynes guides it to point.
On middle, flicked to deep square leg for a single.
On middle, on a length. Defended on the leg side.
FIVE WIDES! Bonus runs! Fuller down the leg side and Lanning misses her flick. The keeper is standing up and that makes her task difficult. Races away to the fence.
Length ball, outside off. Lanning dabs it to the left of third man and comes back for a couple of runs. Good running.
Around off, on a length. Lanning pulls it to mid on.
On a length, on off. Haynes taps it to point and takes off for a quick single.
Looped up, outside off. Lanning leans in and pushes it on the off side.
Sliding into middle nad leg, Rachael Haynes knocks it 'round the corner and picks up a run.
On middle, this is worked towards mid-wicket.
On a length, angling in from outside off. Haynes goes on the back foot to defend it out.
FOUR! More aggression from Rachael Haynes! Flighted delivery, outside off. Haynes steps out and smokes it through extra cover for a glorious boundary. The 100 is up for Australia Women.
Around middle and leg, Rachael Haynes charges down the track and drills it uppishly back past the bowler. The fielder at long on does well to move to her right and cut it off. Two taken.
Short and a bit wide as well. Lanning is unable to take advantage as she taps it straight towards point.
Fullish delivery, angling into middle and leg. Lanning flicks it straight to mid-wicket.
Back of a length, outside off. Haynes guides it past backward point for one more.

Cries of 'Catch it' but the ball falls short. On the pads, Meg Lanning picks it up and whips it towards fine leg. The fielder over there is just a bit slow to react and the ball falls short of her as she dives in. Single taken.
Wide of off again, Haynes does manage to steer it towards backward point for a run this time.

Brunt comes 'around the wicket and hurls across a full ball, outside off. Haynes looks to open the face of the bat and guide it down to third man but gets it all wrong. The ball ends up near cover-point.
This time there is turn! Fuller and outside off. Lanning prods to defend but gets beaten by the turn. A stifled appeal for stumping but Lanning had her back foot grounded.
Tossed up, full and outside off. The ball just holds its line and beats the outside edge of Meg Lanning.
Short and outside off, cut away to point for a single.
Tossed up this time, outside off. Lanning drives it to deep cover for a single.
Full and wide, Lanning taps it towards point.
Nicely flighted, around off. Lanning leans forward and pushes it towards mid off.
Nicely bowled! Cross sees Lanning charging and slows it up. Lanning has to check her heave leg side and just tucks it towards square leg for a run.
In the air...safe! A length ball, around middle and leg. Meg Lanning picks it up and launches it over mid-wicket but the ball clogs into the soggy outfield. They get a couple of runs.
This is angled in from around off. Lanning blocks it out.
Fullish delivery, at a gentle pace and around off. Haynes nudges it on the off side for one.

That seemed close! Around off, Lanning dabs it towards point for a quick single. The throw comes in at the keeper's end but it is a bit wide. Had that been a better throw, Haynes might have been in trouble.
A length ball, on off. This is tapped towards point.
FOUR! Tossed up, around middle. Rachael Haynes skips down the track and just gets enough to get the ball over mid off and she picks up a boundary as well.
Around off, pushed through covers for a single.

Close but not close enough according to the umpire. This is flatter, around middle. Meg Lanning attempts the sweep but misses and gets hit on the pads. Sophie Ecclestone seems a bit interested but the umpire doesn't.
On the pads, tucked away behind square on the leg side for one more.
Loopy delivery, very full and Lanning looks to turn it on the leg side. The ball comes off the toe end of the bat and goes towards cover. They get a single.
Tossed up, full and outside off. Haynes drives to deep cover for a single.
Again short and wide. Lanning slaps but finds the cover fielder. She shakes her head with a cheeky smile as well.
A length ball, width on offer but Lanning fails to clear the infield, the cover region.
Around off, on a length. Lanning with yet another block.
Fuller, straight on middle. Lanning with a defensive prod.
Short again, outside off. Haynes guides it to third man for a single.
Short of a length, around off. Haynes looks to cut but misses.
Outside off. Defended to covers.
Fuller and angling down. Lanning sweeps it to deep square leg and the fielder runs to her right and cuts it off. Two runs taken.
Tossed up, on off. Meg taps it to point.
This one lands on middle and spins away from the right-hander. Defended.
Floated, full, on middle. Blocked out on the front foot.
A flighted ball to start, fuller and on middle. Haynes flicks it uppishly and to mid on for a quick single.
Sophie Ecclestone is now brought into the attack.
FOUR! Good shot! This is just short, not that short but Lanning adjusted really well there as she punches this through cover-point for a boundary. Meg Lanning breaking the shackles here.
Around off, full, pushed to point.
In the air... and safe! Fuller ball, on middle. Haynes has had enough of being defensive as she tries to go big. The ball takes the outside edge and drops well wide of the fielder at point. A single.
Angling on the pads, it is flicked to square leg for a single.
A length ball, jagging back in, on middle. Lanning with a solid block again.
Length and on off. Blocked out.
A slower ball at 105 clicks, fuller and on off, pushed to mid off. Productive over for the Aussies, 7 coming off it.
Outside off, Lanning steers it to third man for a single.
FOUR! First shot of aggression! Full ball, on off. Lanning powers it to long off for a boundary.
Full ball, outside off, pushed back to Sciver.
Fuller and on middle. Haynes shuffles across and whips it to deep square leg for a run.
Length and on off. Lanning on top of the bounce, punches it to the right of point for a quick run.
Length ball, outside off. Haynes pushes with soft hands to covers.
On a length, nipping in, on middle. Lanning is hurried as she pulls it to long on for one.
Angles a full ball, on off. Defended to covers.
A length ball, outside off. Lanning is happy to knock it around, towards point this time.
On a length, outside off, punched off the back foot to covers.
A length ball, outside off. Haynes cuts it to deep backward point for a single.

DRINKS! Australia Women with a watchful start as the pitch is a bit tricky to play. Both Meg Lanning and Rachael Haynes are in a defensive mood but once the ball gets soft, they will unleash themselves. England Women have dominated the opening hour and will look to continue the same way.
Shorter in length and angled well across the left-hander. Haynes looks it behind square on the off side for a single.
Full and wide, this is jammed out towards cover-point.
Fullish delivery, on the pads. Haynes flicks it straight towards mid-wicket.

FOUR! Rachael Haynes was looking for that shot for quite a while now and finally gets the ball to go after. Pitched up, around off. Haynes makes a bit of room, dances down the track and lofts it over wide mid off for a boundary.
Shorter this time and there's a bit of width on offer. Lanning cuts it down to the third man region for a single.
This is full and angling in from around off. Lanning works it towards the cover region.
On off, pushed out towards cover.
Around middle and leg, nudged towards the square leg region.
This is angled on the pads, Lanning clips it down to fine leg and picks up a single.
An inswinger, shaping in nicely from outside off. Lanning keeps it out on the off side.
On off, Haynes makes room and cuts it behind square on the off side for one.
Leg bye! On the pads, Lanning looks to flick it away but the ball comes off the pads and rolls towards mid-wicket. The batters pick up a leg bye.
Full and on off. Haynes blocks it out.
Nicely bowled! A yorker this time, on off and dipping very late. Rachael Haynes does well to get some bat on it.
Back of a length, Meg Lanning hangs back and punches it through cover-point for a single.
A touch shorter, around off. Lanning punches it off the back foot towards cover.
Length again from Sciver and this is angled in from outside off. Lanning stays in her crease and blocks it out on the off side.
A length ball, angled into middle and leg. Lanning tucks it towards mid-wicket.
Fuller this time, around off. Haynes looks for the booming cover drive but ends up defending it out on the off side.
A length delivery, on off. Haynes pushes it gently towards covers.

FIVE WIDES! Kate Cross spills this one down the leg side. Haynes looks to pull it fine but misses and the keeper misses it too. The ball runs away into the fine leg fence and a wide is called as well. Five freebies here for the Aussies.
At a gentle pace and on leg stump. Haynes blocks it under her eyeline.
FOUR! Up and over! Full and wide, Rachael Haynes just makes a bit of room leg side and smashes it inside-out over covers for a lovely boundary.
Around middle and leg this time. Kept out by Haynes.
Kate Cross to bowl now.
A length ball, around the top of middle. Haynes gets right behind the line of the ball to block.
It's full again, around off. Lanning pushes it towards the cover region.
Full, on off. Lanning presses forward to defend it out.
Around leg, Haynes nudges it behind square on the leg side for a run.

SAFE! This is around off and Rachael Haynes just drops it on the off side looking for a quick single. There is a bit of mix-up in the middle and Haynes has to scamper back. The throw comes in and Amy Jones whips off the bails. The decision is sent upstairs and the replays show that Haynes had her bat grounded just in time. NOT OUT!
Run out appeal! The bat is grounded when the stumps are disturbed and Rachael Haynes is NOT OUT! Easy decision there.
Around off and Lanning just opens the face of the bat to guide it through cover-point for one.
A length ball, close to the off pole. This is chopped towards point.
The umpire signals the start of Powerplay 2. As many as 4 fielders can now be stationed outside the inner ring till the 40th over.
Again gets hit on the pads, Rachael Haynes misses here flick but this time it was pitching outside leg. Good over from Rachael Haynes.
A full ball, on the pads. Haynes looks to tuck it but misses and gets hit on the pads. AN appeal for LBW, mostly from the keeper but there was an inside edge on it.
This one slides back in, around off. Meg Lanning gets cramped for room but does well to play it late to third man for one.
A touch fuller and shaping in from around off. Lanning defends it out.
Full and wide, this is squeezed out to point.
This is sliding down the leg side, Haynes works it behind square on the leg side for a single.
The skipper, Meg Lanning is in at number 3.

OUT! TAKEN! England get the breakthrough. Well, the pressure was building and Alyssa Healy had to go big but hold out straight to the fielder. Sciver hurls and serves a fuller delivery, on middle. Alyssa Healy looks to heave it but mistimes her shot completely. The ball might have taken the toe end of her bat as it goes to Katherine Brunt at short mid-wicket who takes a simple catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Katherine Brunt b Natalie Sciver

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and on off, pushed to mid off for a quick single.
On the pads, flicked to deep square leg for a single.

Alyssa Healy has reviewed the LBW decision. It looked a bit high on first glance but the umpire gave it out. The third umpire checks UltraEdge and there is no spike as the ball goes past the bat. Ball Tracker shows that the impact is fine but the ball was going on to miss leg stump. Excellent review from Healy and she survives. The onfield decision is overturned to NOT OUT.

NOT OUT! The first thought was it was nipping down the leg side but the umpire took her time before raising her finger. This is on a length and angling on the pads. Alyssa Healy looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads. An appeal and the umpire raises her dreaded finger after thinking for a while. It looked like it was missing the stumps and Alyssa Healy after consulting her partner takes it upstairs. Wickets missing though. Good review from Alyssa Healy.
Fullish delivery, outside off, pushed straight to mid off.
Full ball, slanting away, outside off. Blocked out.
Wide! Sciver errs in her line as she starts with a loose one. Down the leg side. Left alone.
Fuller and outside off. Haynes mistimes her push to covers.
Length ball, around off. Haynes inside edges her drive onto the pads.
Good length! Anything short and Australia are getting on it. England have to keep the length near to the batter. Around off. Kept out.
Shorter and on middle, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Touch fuller, outside off. Healy is late to push but does well to play it along the ground. It is a hard pitch to bat on and Australia Women will be happy, they have not lost a wicket yet.
Short of a length, outside off. Healy defends with soft hands and the ball rolls over to his pads.
Slightly short and Healy gets on top of it, as she pulls it to deep square leg for a single.
Almost chopped on! Fuller ball, around off, it nips back in a touch. Healy looks to push but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
FOUR! Loosener! Short ball, on middle. Healy pulls it to square leg for a boundary. This will release some pressure on Healy.
This one just seamed away. On a length, on off. Haynes defends with soft hands and edges it away to third man for a single.
Around off. Haynes keeps it out to point.
Length ball, angling on the pads, nudged to square leg.

In the air but safe! Fuller ball, outside off. Healy is early as she tries to go over mid off and toe ends it. The ball just drops to the right of covers and races away through mid off for a couple of runs. Dot balls are building pressure here. Really good start by England Women.
Touch fuller, outside off, Healy taps it to covers.
A length ball, outside off, not much movement there and Healy misses her push.
Outside off. Healy dabs it nicely but straight to backward point.
On a length, outside off. Alyssa stays back to defend it out. Australia are cautious with their start.
Full ball, swinging back, on off. Healy tucks it to mid-wicket.
Angles it on the pads, flicked to mid-wicket.
On a length, nipping back in, around off. Haynes plays close to the pads and defends it.
On a length, on off. Blocked out.
A length ball, outside off. Healy drops it to covers for a single.
Around off, pushed to point.
On the pads, Haynes flicks it through square leg for a single.
A length ball, on off. This is blocked out by Healy.
Not timed this time! Pitched up, on middle. Healy lofts it over mid-wicket and picks up a brace.
This is angled into middle and leg. Healy tucks it towards mid-wicket.
FOUR! Aggressive intent from Alyssa Healy! Full and on the pads, Healy steps down the track and whips it over mid-wicket. The ball races away into the fence.
Full, around off. Healy leans in and pushes it out on the off side.
WIDE! This is spilled down the leg side. Wide called.
FOUR! Full and wide, this is nicely driven by Healy. She pierces the gap through the cover region and finds the fence.
This is pushed wider, Healy chops it towards point for a single.
FOUR! Short of a length but not short enough. Alyssa Healy hangs back and short-arm jabs it into the square leg fence.
Length again, on off and shaping away. Healy gets right behind the line of the ball to block.

A length ball, around off and Healy pushes it out towards covers. It looks like the bowler, Katherine Brunt wants the keeper to stand up to the stumps now. She is sensing that Healy wants to charge down the track.
Back of a length, outside off. Healy looks to swipe across the line but mistimes it badly towards mid on.
On the pads, flicked down to fine leg for one.
Huge in-dipper this time, swinging onto the pads. Alyssa Healy whips it with the swing and picks up a couple of runs towards deep square leg.
Shaping back in from outside off. Healy blocks it out.
Full and straight, this is firmly driven but straight to mid on.
Good-length ball, around leg. Haynes tucks it away to square leg for a quick single.
Length again, wide outside off this time. Australia Women and Alyssa Healy are off the mark with an edge down to third man.
A length ball, swinging back in from well outside off. Healy nudges it on the off side.
Who will start from the other end? Anya Shrubsole it is.
Brunt starts off with a maiden! Around middle and shaping back in. Haynes defends it out.
On the pads, flicked away to mid-wicket.
A touch fuller again and wide of off. Rachael Haynes lets it through to the keeper.
Fuller this time, angled across the left-hander. Haynes leaves it alone.
Right around the top of off stump. Rachael Haynes stays solid in defense.
A hint of movement on offer for Katherine Brunt. On a length, around middle and shaping back into the left-hander. Haynes defends it out.

We are all set. The players walk out to the middle. Rachael Haynes and Alyssa Healy are the openers of Australia Women. The English players take a knee to support the Black Lives Matter movement.  Katherine Brunt to start with the ball. Here we go ...

The players of both the respected teams line up together as there will be a minute silence seen as a mark of respect to the passing away of Shane Warne and Rod Marsh. Now, the national anthems will be played... The players will wear a black armband as well.

England Women (Playing XI) - Lauren Winfield, Tammy Beaumont, Heather Knight (C), Natalie Sciver, Amy Jones (WK), Danni Wyatt, Sophia Dunkley, Katherine Brunt, Sophie Ecclestone, Kate Cross, Anya Shrubsole.

Australia Women (Playing XI) - Alyssa Healy (WK), Rachael Haynes, Meg Lanning (C), Ellyse Perry, Beth Mooney, Tahlia McGrath, Annabel Sutherland, Jess Jonassen, Alana King, Megan Schutt, Darcie Brown.
TOSS - Up goes the coin and it lands in the favour of England Women. They have elected to BOWL first!

England Women are the defending champions and they could not have a more difficult game to get their title defense underway than this one. After being humbled by their opponents in the Women's Ashes ODIs about a couple of months earlier, Heather Knight will be looking to get her team all fired up in order to get revenge and what better stage than the biggest stage of them all to do it. The English side is filled with exciting young talent mixed with bundles of experience but they have their work cut out in front of them today. But will the English be able to get past the mighty Aussies? Or will Australia sweep aside their rivals? We'll find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit.

The Australian team have been in red-hot form over the last 30 matches, having lost just once and after a clean sweep at the Women's Ashes ODIs, Meg Lanning and her team will be confident of inflicting yet another blow to their biggest rivals and get the tournament underway with a win. The six-time World Champions will be looking to regain the title this time around and there will be no surprises if they do so but first, they have to get over this hurdle.

Hello and a warm welcome to Match number 3 of the ICC Women's World Cup from Seddon Park in Hamilton. In the second clash of Super Saturday, two stalwarts of the Women's game go head to head as Australia Women take on arch-rivals England Women in what will be a tasty encounter. Both teams have been prolific in this tournament having won the title 10 times between them but only one can take bragging rights today.
